jobs.title: Associate Director, Automation & Innovation
jobs.description:
At AstraZeneca, we pride ourselves on crafting a collaborative culture that champions knowledge-sharing, ambitious thinking and innovation – ultimately providing employees with the opportunity to work across teams, functions and even the globe.

Recognizing the importance of individualized flexibility, our ways of working allow employees to balance personal and work commitments while ensuring we continue to create a strong culture of collaboration and teamwork by engaging face-to-face in our offices 3 days a week. Our head office and BlueSky Hub in downtown Toronto are purposely designed with collaboration in mind, providing space where teams can come together to strategize, brainstorm and connect on key projects.

Our dedication to sustainability is also central to our culture and part of what makes AstraZeneca a great place to work. We know the health of people, the planet and our business are interconnected which is why we’re taking ambitious action to tackle some of the biggest challenges of our time, from climate change to access to healthcare and disease prevention.

Are you ready to harness AI to reshape how a portfolio of life-changing medicines is delivered to patients? Do you see yourself translating the latest advances in AI, machine learning and NLP into decisions that accelerate development and sharpen our strategic focus across a global R&D portfolio?

In this role, you will set direction and drive adoption of enterprise AI initiatives that unlock value in project and portfolio management, decision support, capacity planning and governance. You will join a high-performing team that connects data, processes and technology to reveal new insights, reduce cycle times and improve the way critical portfolio decisions are made—always with patient impact in mind.

Working alongside product, data, IT, compliance and business leaders, you will move from pilots to scaled capabilities that are ethical, secure and compliant, ensuring AI becomes a trusted, measurable accelerator for our pipeline and operations.

Accountabilities

AI Strategy Leadership: Define and communicate an actionable AI strategy aligned to business objectives, setting clear priorities and success measures across portfolio, functional and tactical levels.
Opportunity Discovery: Identify high-impact AI use cases in project management, portfolio analytics and decision support, capacity management and governance, translating pain points into solution roadmaps.
Roadmap and Delivery: Lead design, pilots and scaled deployments of AI solutions; sequence investments, manage risks and ensure delivery excellence from proof of concept to enterprise adoption.
Value Realization and KPIs: Establish metrics, dashboards and review cadences to track performance, adoption and ROI; course-correct to maximize impact on cycle time, quality and decision speed.
Responsible AI and Compliance: Embed privacy, security, ethics and regulatory requirements in solution design and operations; ensure alignment with standards such as GDPR, HIPAA and EMA guidance.
Partnership Building: Orchestrate cross-functional collaboration with IT, data science, business units, legal and compliance; manage external relationships with vendors, academia and industry consortia.
Change Leadership and Adoption: Champion innovation and knowledge sharing; enable training, communications and change management that build trust and scale new ways of working.
Modern Data and Architecture: Guide choices on data pipelines, model lifecycle management and governance to ensure solutions are robust, reusable and resilient.
External Representation: Stay ahead of industry trends; represent the organization in forums and communities to bring back insights and influence best practice.
Progressive Impact: Deliver early wins in priority domains, then scale patterns across the platform to improve portfolio delivery, strengthen decision-making and contribute to faster patient impact.

Essential Skills/Experience

Advanced degree in Computer/Data/AI/Engineering or a related quantitative field; Bachelor’s with equivalent experience considered. Minimum 6+ years experience
Extensive hands-on experience with AI/ML/NLP and analytics, including model development, deployment and lifecycle management; familiarity with modern data architecture and governance.
Proven delivery of AI strategies and solutions at scale in regulated environments (pharma/healthcare preferred), translating digital technologies into measurable business impact; PPM experience in Life Sciences is mandatory.
Demonstrated leadership of cross-functional, global teams and complex programs; strong business acumen, stakeholder management and communication skills for technical and non-technical audiences; evidence of thought leadership in AI/innovation.
Deep understanding of data governance, privacy and ethics with working familiarity of GDPR, HIPAA and EMA guidance.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capability, able to synthesize complex data and present clear insights to senior leadership
Customer-focused, adaptable and results-driven; self-starter who works effectively both independently and in global, cross-functional settings

Desirable Skills/Experience

Certifications in AI, data science, or project management (such as Certified Data Professional, PMP, or equivalent)

jobs.title: Director, Engineering Performance & AI Metrics
jobs.description:
What You'll Do

The Director, Engineering Performance & AI Metrics
defines how the organization measures engineering and agile delivery performance at scale, with a specific focus on how “performance” changes as AI becomes embedded in agile ways of working. This role is accountable for establishing an Agile & AI performance measurement practice, including the standards, tooling, governance, visualization and story-telling, team structure, and operating routines needed to measure delivery flow, predictability, quality, business value, and the impact of GenAI and automation.

Core Accountabilities

Establish and lead the Agile & AI performance measurement practice, including its operating model, governance, standards, team capability, and roadmap.
Define enterprise measurement frameworks for agile delivery and AI-enabled ways of working, covering flow, predictability, quality, value realization, team health, adoption, and productivity impact.
Augment traditional agile performance metrics with new KPIs that reflect total system health in an agentic landscape, including human-AI collaboration, automation effectiveness, work orchestration, quality signals, risk, governance, and team sustainability.
Own the Engineering performance analytics platform strategy and roadmap, including data quality, governance, tooling integration, investment recommendations, and scalable visibility across engineering and agile delivery.
Translate performance data into executive-ready stories that connect trends, risks, systemic bottlenecks, investment decisions, delivery trade-offs, transformation progress, and improvement opportunities.
Partner across engineering, delivery, finance, transformation, and agile leadership to connect performance insights to business outcomes and operating model decisions.
Ensure metrics are used responsibly, with enough context to support learning, transparency, and continuous improvement rather than activity tracking or simplistic team comparisons.
Build and lead a high-performing performance measurement and insights practice, including role design, talent development, delivery model, and capability roadmap.

What You Bring

10+ years of experience in agile delivery, delivery excellence, transformation, product operations, performance measurement, or related roles.
Ability to assess AI adoption and impact responsibly, including metric limitations, false precision, quality, risk, governance, and team health.
Strong understanding of agile operating models, scaled delivery practices, agile metrics, and executive performance story-telling to support decision-making
Deep expertise in engineering productivity and delivery performance frameworks such as SPACE and DORA, with demonstrated ability to adapt them to enterprise-scale Agile and AI-enabled delivery environments.
Demonstrated ability to establish enterprise standards and frameworks, analysis structure and strategic visualization, and insight routines that drive practical improvement.
Proven ability to translate complex engineering, delivery, and AI adoption signals into executive-level insights that influence prioritization, investment, risk management, and operating model decisions, using enterprise delivery and analytics platforms including Power BI, Atlassian, and other engineering tools
Strong practical understanding of GenAI, agentic AI, automation, and AI-enabled software delivery, including how these capabilities change work patterns, delivery flow, developer experience, quality, productivity, and value realization.

We may use artificial intelligence tools as part of our recruitment process to assist in the initial screening of resumes. All hiring decisions, including candidate evaluation, selection, and disposition, are made by human recruiters.

About Us

Canadian Tire Corporation, Limited (“CTC”) is one of Canada’s most admired and trusted companies. With more than 90 Owned Brands, over 1,600 retail locations, financial services, exemplary e-commerce capabilities, and exciting market-leading merchandising strategies. We dream big and work as one to innovate with purpose for our customers at every level of our business, investing in new technologies and products, and doubling down on top talent to drive the company forward. We offer competitive salaries and wages to CTC employees, as well as store discounts, supported learning through our Triangle Learning Academy, Canadian Tire Profit Sharing, and retirement and savings programs for eligible employees. As part of our enhanced flex benefits program, we offer mental health benefits in the amount of $5,000 per year for benefits-eligible employees and their families, including total well-being, and mental health tools and resources for all employees. Join us in helping to make life in Canada better through living and working our Core Values: we are innovators and entrepreneurs at our core, outcomes drive us, inclusion is a must, we are stronger together and we take personal responsibility. It is an especially exciting time to join CTC and its family of companies where career opportunities are wide-ranging! Join us, where there's a place for you here.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging

We are committed to fostering an environment where belonging thrives, and diversity, inclusion and equity are infused into everything we do. We believe in building an organizational culture where people are consistently treated with dignity while respecting individual religion, nationality, gender, race, age, perceived ability, spoken language, sexual orientation, and identification. We are united in our purpose of being here to help make life in Canada better.

Accommodations

We stand firm in our Core Value that inclusion is a must. We welcome and encourage candidates from equity-seeking groups such as people who identify as racialized, Indigenous, 2SLGBTQIA+, women, people with disabilities, and beyond. Should you require any accommodation in applying for this role, or throughout the interview process, please make them known when contacted and we will work with you to help meet your needs.

jobs.title: AVP, GTO Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
As AVP, GTO Strategy & Transformation, you will lead GTO's strategy, transformation agenda, and multi-year roadmap, while also overseeing the GTO global AI platform roadmap. Your focus will be on shaping where GTO is going and ensuring its transformation delivers measurable business value. You will lead multi-year strategy development, operating model transformation, AI enablement, value realization, workforce modernization, and enterprise-scale transformation initiatives. Working closely with Technology, Operations, Finance, People Partners, and business leaders, you will identify opportunities to redesign how work gets done, convert productivity gains into measurable business outcomes, and help build an AI-enabled growth engine that supports growth while maintaining expense discipline. This is an AI-native team — the team uses AI tools, agentic workflows, and LLM-connected platforms as its primary way of working, not as an occasional add-on.

Position Responsibilities

GTO Strategy & Strategic Planning: Lead development of multi-year GTO strategy, transformation roadmaps, investment priorities, and strategic planning processes. Translate enterprise objectives into executable plans across Technology and Operations, ensuring strategic intent is reflected in investment and delivery decisions before resources are committed.
AI-Native Operating Model Transformation: Design and evolve future-state operating models that combine AI, automation, workforce transformation, and technology productivity to sustainably improve capacity, customer outcomes, and efficiency across Technology and Operations — including delivery models, product operating models, workforce structures, and technology ways of working.
Technology Productivity Realization: Partner with CIOs, COOs, and segment leaders to identify, quantify, and realize value from technology productivity improvements — including product operating models, engineering productivity, and delivery modernization — ensuring productivity gains translate into measurable operational and business outcomes rather than remaining theoretical.
Operational Transformation & Value Realization: Lead enterprise operational transformation initiatives across customer service, operations, digital channels, workforce productivity, and support functions. Current focus areas may include contact centre transformation, containment optimization, service modernization, and AI-enabled efficiency programs — with the underlying methodology (diagnostic rigor, cross-source data reconciliation, quantified business cases) designed to generalize to future transformation priorities as GTO's agenda evolves.
Workforce Transformation & Future Skills: Define workforce transition strategies, future-skill requirements, role redesign opportunities, and redeployment approaches required to support AI-enabled operating models. Partner with People Partners, L&D, and segment leaders to drive execution — setting direction, tracking progress, and identifying opportunities to accelerate adoption in partnership with segment leaders.
Enterprise Value Realization: Own benefit targets and KPI commitments across the GTO transformation portfolio. Establish and govern enterprise value realization methodologies, validate assumptions, reconcile benefit calculations across data sources, create defensible performance baselines, and ensure reported outcomes remain transparent and defensible to senior leadership and ELT — explicitly separating transformation-driven impact from organic or external trends.
Product & Portfolio Leadership Strengthened: Own and evolve the GTO AI product roadmap, defining priorities and sequencing releases across initiatives and reusable capabilities. Ensure product investments align with GTO strategic priorities and target-state operating model objectives, rather than being pursued independently of the broader transformation agenda.
Executive & Board-Level Narrative Ownership: Own the preparation of ELT and Board/Technology Committee-ready materials — portfolio checkpoints, anticipated-Q&A briefs, and strategic narratives — translating complex, multi-segment operational and financial data into clear, decision-ready formats. Anticipate scrutiny across every segment and function represented, not just the primary owner's area, and ensure diplomatic, precise, and defensible framing throughout.
GTO Global AI Platform Roadmap Ownership: Own and oversee the GTO global AI platform roadmap — set the AI direction and transformation agenda for GTO across 14 countries, translate enterprise AI vision into operational priorities, and ensure the platform roadmap is directly sequenced against GTO's broader multi-year strategy and transformation agenda rather than developed in isolation. Apply strategic rigour to problem framing and solution design, ensuring the right problems are prioritized before delivery resources are committed, and assess strategic AI hypotheses through structured pilots prior to scaling investment.
Outcome Measurement: Establish clear success measures — adoption, operational impact, cycle-time improvements, reliability — and report progress to senior leadership.
Delivery Execution: Lead end-to-end delivery planning and execution for approved transformation and AI initiatives, ensuring predictable release rhythms and timely removal of blockers.
Competitive Intelligence: Maintain ongoing awareness of AI and transformation developments across financial services and the broader enterprise landscape. Translate external signals — competitor moves, emerging capabilities, regulatory shifts — into strategic implications for the GTO agenda.
Production Readiness: Drive readiness reviews with Technology, Enterprise AI, and Risk partners to confirm controls, documentation, and deployment plans are in place prior to release.
Cross-functional Escalation: Act as escalation point for delivery throughput issues, coordinating cross-functional resolution and trade-off decisions.
Platform Reuse & Scaling: Lead the shift from project-by-project delivery to a reusable capability model — shared components, templates, evaluation patterns, and connectors.
Governance Alignment: Ensure solutions align with Responsible AI and model risk expectations, including appropriate documentation and monitoring plans.
Opportunity Identification & Prioritization: Identify, quantify, and prioritize AI and operational-transformation opportunities across GTO using structured analysis and operational input — including digital-capability heatmapping, deflection/containment sizing, and repeat-contact root-cause analysis. Build data-driven business cases with Finance and Operations leaders, using the same rigor applied to product investment decisions.
Transformation Investment Prioritization: Evaluate strategic initiatives, validate business cases, recommend investment priorities, and support trade-off decisions across the GTO portfolio.
Executive Decision Support & Strategic Communications:Serve as a primary architect of executive decision support across GTO — ELT materials, Board and Technology Committee narratives, investor-facing content, anticipated-Q&A preparation, and strategic storyline development. Treat this as a defining capability of the function, not a byproduct of other work: the quality of this synthesis directly shapes how senior leadership and the Board understand GTO's transformation progress.
AI-First Operating Model: Lead by example in how the team works. Personally use LLM-connected agents, enterprise agentic AI platforms, and AI-augmented workflows to reimagine how portfolio reporting, strategy synthesis, operational diagnostics, and executive communications are produced — including live querying of enterprise data platforms to validate findings in real time. Set the standard for the team and demonstrate that AI-first ways of working are operational — not aspirational.
People Leadership: Build and lead a high-performing team focused on operational discipline, delivery excellence, and continuous improvement.

Required Qualifications

Experience leading enterprise strategy, operating model redesign, or large-scale transformation efforts across Technology, Operations, or shared services environments.
10+ years of experience in strategy, transformation leadership, product leadership, technology delivery, platform programs, and/or AI-enabled transformation, preferably in regulated industries.
Proven track record delivering complex products, transformation programs, or platforms into production with measurable outcomes, including release planning and dependency management.
Experience operating at enterprise scale across multiple geographies or business units, including setting targets and holding accountability for benefit realization.
Demonstrated experience in operational analytics — diagnosing performance issues from raw operational data, reconciling discrepancies across data sources, and translating findings into funded business cases.
Strong ability to lead cross-functionally in matrixed environments and communicate clearly with senior stakeholders.
Strong experience in quantitative modeling, scenario analysis, and business case development.
Working knowledge of modern AI solution patterns (e.g., LLM-enabled assistants, intelligent document processing, agent-based workflows) and production readiness considerations.
Hands-on orientation with AI productivity tools and agentic workflows; personally comfortable using LLM-connected enterprise tools — including direct querying of enterprise data platforms — to accelerate strategy, reporting, and synthesis work.
Experience working with executive leadership teams, Boards, Technology Committees, or governance forums to support strategic decision-making.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience evolving operating models from project-based to product/platform delivery.
Familiarity with MLOps/LLMOps concepts, evaluation approaches, monitoring, and model governance practices.
Experience influencing people strategy, workforce transformation, or AI reskilling programs in a tech/operations context.
Demonstrated ability to validate strategic hypotheses through pilots and translate early wins into enterprise momentum.
Experience with contact centre or operations analytics — IVR/self-service containment, FCR/repeat-contact analysis, workforce management metrics — in a multi-country or multi-segment environment.
Advanced degree or equivalent experience in engineering, computer science, data science, or business.

When You Join Our Team

We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.
As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.
